title: Marguerite and the Vow
premise: Marguerite Voss, archivist and heir to her grandmother's failing seaside hotel, is assigned an anonymous pen-pal correspondence through a coastal literacy program — only to discover her letters are going to Silas Thackeray, the marine biologist whose family once tried to buy and demolish her grandmother's property. Bound by the program's rules of anonymity, the two enemies fall in love on paper while waging open war in person over the hotel's future. When Marguerite's grandmother's will gives her one year to make the hotel profitable or lose it to the Thackeray trust, and Silas is offered a research post abroad, both must decide whether the vow they made to the dead outweighs the one they never made to each other. The story ends when the final anonymous letter is revealed, the hotel is saved as a joint marine-research retreat, and Silas misses his flight to stay past the last train.
about_author: Jonah Ashgrove is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who spent seven years cataloguing letters found in coastal inns along the Atlantic seaboard. He writes slow-burn romances about people who mistake stubbornness for solitude.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Lies
chapters.summary: Silas Thackeray's POV. A marine biologist who treats the heart as a trainable muscle returns to Saltmere Bay to oversee his family trust's claim on the Voss hotel, counting sea turtles to avoid counting his losses. He coldly signs up for the literacy program's pen-pal outreach as a PR gesture. Emotional beat: armored loneliness disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: Ink and Inheritance
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite inherits a hotel drowning in debt and a will demanding one profitable year, then grudgingly joins the same pen-pal program to fulfill the will's 'community engagement' clause. She writes her first anonymous letter as an act of defiance, not hope. Emotional beat: grief for her grandmother hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Enemies by Day, Strangers by Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In person, Silas serves Marguerite the trust's demolition notice; on paper, 'S' and 'M' exchange startlingly honest letters about loss and the sea. Each begins to suspect — then dismisses — the truth of who the other is. Emotional beat: the delicious dramatic irony of intimacy growing inside hostility.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brings In
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A storm floods the hotel's basement, and Silas — anonymously, off the clock — helps her salvage her grandmother's letters, including evidence the Thackerays once loved the Voss family. He leaves before she can thank him. Emotional beat: a crack in the armor; the first involuntary tenderness.

chapters.title: The Train Timetable
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas receives the overseas research offer he's wanted for a decade, with a departure date weeks away. He tells his pen-pal 'M' about it before anyone else, and her reply — 'some vows are just fear wearing a suit' — unsettles him. Emotional beat: ambition revealed as escape.

chapters.title: Almost, On Paper
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The pen-pals agree to meet at the midsummer festival, each planning to arrive early and identify the other. Both lose their nerve at the last moment and watch each other from across the square, each believing the other never came. Emotional beat: heartbreak from a near-miss neither understands.

chapters.title: The Clause in the Will
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite discovers the will's fine print: the Thackeray trust holds the mortgage, meaning Silas has been her landlord-destroyer all along — and that her grandmother knew, and left a sealed letter for 'whoever she loves enough to stay.' Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as a question she can't yet answer.

chapters.title: Confessions at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas realizes 'M' is Marguerite when he recognizes her phrasing from the demolition meeting. He confesses everything in a final anonymous letter, then goes to her in person to resign from the trust — and finds her holding his letter, furious and shaking. Emotional beat: the climax of exposure; love and betrayal in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Vow, Reconsidered
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. On the eve of Silas's flight and the trust's final deadline, Marguerite reads her grandmother's sealed letter: the Vows and Thackerays were once engaged, split by the same choice between duty and love, and the will was a test, not a trap. Marguerite races to rewrite the ending. Emotional beat: choosing love as inheritance, not its betrayal.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Silas stands at the station as the last train pulls away without him; Marguerite arrives with the trust renegotiated — the hotel becomes a marine-research retreat under both names, and the pen-pal program's final letters are read aloud at its reopening. He stays. Emotional beat: the vow kept by being broken; home chosen over escape.
